title: Sandy Beaches in Mljet 2027: Saplunara, Blace & Pebble
metaDescription: Mljet has real sand, but only in the far southeast: Velika and Mala Saplunara and Blace. Surface, shallows, shade, parking and alternatives near Dubrovnik.
content:
## Does Mljet Have Sandy Beaches?

Mljet has real sand, but very little of it, and all of it sits in one place: the Saplunara area at the southeastern end of the island. Most of the coastline is rock, so Mljet is not a sand-and-sunbed island. Pebble, rock ledges and concrete bathing platforms dominate everywhere else. If sand is the priority, base yourself in or near Saplunara. If you only come for a day from Dubrovnik, sand is possible but costs a lot of travel time.

## Beach Surface on Mljet at a Glance

| Area | Surface | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Velika Saplunara | Sand | Southeast tip |
| Mala Saplunara | Sand | Southeast tip |
| Blace (Limuni) | Sand | East of Saplunara |
| Sutmiholjska | Fine pebble | South coast |
| Pomena and Polače (national park side) | Rock and concrete platforms | Northwest |

## The Real Sandy Beaches on Mljet

### Velika Saplunara (sand)
Saplunara is a bay about 1 km long with a pine forest behind it. The name comes from the Latin word for sand. Velika ("large") Saplunara is the busiest of the sandy beaches, and also the most developed, with seasonal services in summer.

- **Surface:** fine sand.
- **Water for children:** very shallow and warm. This is the best choice on the island for toddlers and weak swimmers.
- **Shade:** natural shade from pines at the back of the beach. Umbrellas are still useful in the middle of the day.
- **Crowds:** the busiest sand beach on Mljet, but still small by Croatian standards. Mid-July to late August is the peak.
- **Parking:** free, informal roadside and gravel parking beside the main island road. Arrive before 10:00 in August.

### Mala Saplunara (sand)
Mala ("small") Saplunara is the same kind of sand with a quieter feel and fewer services. It is a short walk from Velika Saplunara. The slope into the water is similarly gentle, and the pines give the same shade. Bring water and snacks, because shops in Saplunara are limited.

### Blace / Limuni (sand)
Blace, also called Limuni, is the most natural of the three. It is a protected sandy bay of roughly 800 m, and the water in it is shallow, warm and lagoon-like. The walk from Saplunara takes about 20 minutes, and there is little or no infrastructure at the end of it. The area is protected landscape, so take rubbish out with you. It is also known as an informal naturist spot, which matters for some families. Walk in the morning or late afternoon, because there is little shade along the way in July and August.

**Opinion:** Blace is worth the walk, but only if you carry water. A hot midday walk with small children and no shop at the end is a mistake that is easy to avoid.

## The Best Fine-Pebble Beach: Sutmiholjska

Sutmiholjska lies on the south coast, outside the national park, between Ropa and Babino Polje. The beach is pebble, with a deep, tiny bay and a very gentle entry into the sea. That makes it comfortable for children even though it is not sand. A restaurant, small shop and rental point operate in season. Shade is limited, so an umbrella is needed. Reach it by car or taxi from Sobra, Polače or Pomena. Parking is informal and free. It is calmer than Saplunara on most days, and popular with locals from Babino Polje.

## Rock and Concrete: The National Park Side

Pomena, Polače and the shores of the Salt Lakes are about rocks and concrete platforms with ladders, not sand. The water is very clear and good for swimming, but entry is steep or slippery in places. Water shoes are advisable. These spots suit confident swimmers and are poor for toddlers.

## How to Get to Saplunara and Blace

1. **Ferry to Sobra:** Jadrolinija runs car and passenger ferries from Dubrovnik (Gruž) and from Prapratno on the Pelješac peninsula. Sobra is the main arrival port for Saplunara.
2. **Sobra to Saplunara:** about 20 km along the main island road, roughly 30 minutes by car. Public bus and taxi are available but infrequent, so check the day's timetable.
3. **Car:** the most flexible option. Fill the tank before leaving Sobra, as fuel stations on Mljet are few.
4. **Blace:** park at Saplunara and walk about 20 minutes.

Saplunara is far from the national park at the other end of the island. Plan accommodation near the sand if beach time is the priority.

## Nearest Other Real Sandy Beaches

- **Šunj, Lopud:** the best-known true sand near Dubrovnik. Ferry from Dubrovnik (Gruž) to Lopud takes about 50 minutes. From Lopud town, allow a 20-30 minute walk or a short golf-cart ride across the island. Water is shallow and the beach has a seasonal bar and shade from trees at the back.
- **Saplunara from Dubrovnik:** a day trip is possible but long. Allow roughly 1 hour 45 minutes by ferry plus the 30-minute drive. This is manageable for an overnight stay and tiring as a single day.

For travellers who want sand and have only one day, Lopud is the more efficient choice. For travellers with 2 or more nights, Saplunara is better.

## Practical Tips for Sand Seekers

- Book accommodation in Saplunara if you want to walk to the beach. Most other stays on Mljet are far from sand.
- The bay faces southwest, so it is sheltered from the bura and maestral winds. The southwest wind can raise waves, so check the forecast.
- Bring your own shade, water and food for Blace and Mala Saplunara.
- Sand beaches are free. Umbrella and sunbed rental, where offered, is seasonal.

## Verdict: Is Mljet Good for People Who Want Sand?

Mljet suits sand lovers only if they accept a small, specific area. The Saplunara bay and Blace give real, shallow, family-friendly sand with pine shade, and few places in Croatia match that calm. The rest of the island is rock and pebble, so it is a poor choice for anyone expecting sand wherever they stay. Pick Saplunara for sand, Sutmiholjska for gentle pebble, and the national park side for clear water and rocks. If you only want a quick sandy afternoon from Dubrovnik, Šunj on Lopud is faster.

faq.question: Does Mljet have a sandy beach?
faq.answer: Yes. Velika Saplunara, Mala Saplunara and Blace (Limuni) are real sandy beaches at the southeastern end of the island. The rest of Mljet is mainly rock, concrete platforms and pebble.

faq.question: What is the best beach on Mljet for small children?
faq.answer: Velika Saplunara is the easiest, with very shallow sand and pine shade. Sutmiholjska is the best non-sand alternative, as it is a fine-pebble beach with a very gentle entry.

faq.question: How do I get to Blace (Limuni) beach?
faq.answer: Drive or take a taxi to Saplunara, park near the bay and walk about 20 minutes. There are few facilities at Blace, so bring water, food and sun protection.

faq.question: Is there parking at Saplunara?
faq.answer: Yes, parking is free and informal, along the road and on gravel areas near the bay. It fills up in July and August, so arrive before 10:00.

faq.question: Where is the nearest sandy beach to Mljet besides Saplunara?
faq.answer: Šunj on Lopud is the closest well-known true sandy beach. The ferry from Dubrovnik (Gruž) takes about 50 minutes, followed by a 20-30 minute walk.

faq.question: Can I visit Saplunara as a day trip from Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: It is possible but long, with about 1 hour 45 minutes by ferry to Sobra and then about 30 minutes by car. An overnight stay in Saplunara is more comfortable.

quickAnswer: Yes, Mljet has real sand, but only at the far southeastern tip: Velika Saplunara, Mala Saplunara and Blace (Limuni). Everywhere else on the island is rock, concrete platforms or pebble. Sutmiholjska is the best fine-pebble beach. The nearest other true sand is Šunj on Lopud, about 50 minutes by ferry from Dubrovnik.
